```{r}
library(palmerpenguins)
library(ggplot2)
library(maps)
library(sf)
#insert introduction commentary here
```
```{r}
ncol(penguins)
nrow(penguins)
pmale <- penguins[penguins$sex == "male",]
pfemale <- penguins[penguins$sex == "female",]
nrow(pmale)
nrow(pfemale)
#There are 179 male penguins and 176 female penguins. Pretty even split!
padel <- penguins[penguins$species == "Adelie",]
pchin <- penguins[penguins$species == "Chinstrap",]
pgen <- penguins[penguins$species == "Gentoo",]
nrow(padel)
nrow(pchin)
nrow(pgen)
#There are 152 Adelie penguins, 68 Chinstrap penguins, and 124 Gentoo penguins. The Adelie penguins are the most common species in this dataset.
ibis <- penguins[penguins$island == "Biscoe",]
idream <- penguins[penguins$island == "Dream",]
itorg <- penguins[penguins$island == "Torgersen",]
nrow(ibis)
nrow(idream)
nrow(itorg)
#There are 168 penguins on Biscoe, 124 penguins on Dream, and 52 penguins on Torgersen. Biscoe is the most common island in this dataset.
```
```{r}
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = sex, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_col(aes(color = sex)) +
  labs(title = "Body Mass of Penguins by Sex",
       x = "Sex",
       y = "Body Mass (g)") +
  theme_minimal()
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm)) +
  geom_col(aes(color = species)) +
  labs(title = "Flipper Length of Penguins by Species",
       x = "Species",
       y = "Flipper Length (mm)") +
  theme_minimal()
  ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = island, y = species)) +
  geom_col(aes(color = species), size = 3) +
  labs(title = "Penguin Species by Island",
       x = "Island",
       y = "Species") +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r FINALsex}
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = sex, y = body_mass_g)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(color = sex), width = 0.3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#ff5ea6","#4e86ff")) +
  labs(x = "Sex",
       y = "Body Mass (g)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r FINALspecies}
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = species, y = flipper_length_mm)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(color = species), width = 0.3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#d72a0b","#3f9c09","#0ca0a0")) +
  labs(x = "Species",
       y = "Flipper Length (mm)") +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r FINALisland}
ggplot(data = penguins, aes(x = species, y = island)) +
  geom_boxplot(aes(color = species), width = 0.3, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_jitter(aes(color = species), alpha = 0.5, show.legend = FALSE, position = position_jitter(width = 0.2, seed = 0)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("#f99010","#a119f6","#0ca0a0")) +
  labs(x = "Species",
       y = "Island") +
  theme_minimal()
```


```{r ANTARCTICA_AI BUILT}
#This map was built entirely by the sidebar AI, I'm just trying to see what the packages can do
antarctica_map <- maps::map("world", regions = "Antarctica", fill = TRUE, plot = FALSE)
valid_points <- !is.na(antarctica_map$x) & !is.na(antarctica_map$y)
segments <- split(
  which(valid_points),
  cumsum(!valid_points)[valid_points] + 1
)

antarctica_sf <- sf::st_sf(
  name = antarctica_map$names,
  geometry = sf::st_sfc(
    lapply(segments, function(index) {
      sf::st_polygon(list(cbind(antarctica_map$x[index], antarctica_map$y[index])))
    }),
    crs = 4326
  )
)
antarctica_sf <- sf::st_transform(antarctica_sf, crs = 3031)

island_coordinates <- data.frame(
  island = c("Biscoe", "Dream", "Torgersen"),
  longitude = c(-65.500, -64.233, -64.083),
  latitude = c(-65.433, -64.733, -64.767)
)
penguin_counts <- as.data.frame(table(penguins$island, penguins$species))
names(penguin_counts) <- c("island", "species", "count")
penguin_counts <- subset(penguin_counts, count > 0)
penguin_counts <- merge(penguin_counts, island_coordinates, by = "island")

island_locations <- sf::st_as_sf(
  island_coordinates,
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
  crs = 4326
)
island_locations <- sf::st_transform(island_locations, crs = 3031)
penguin_points_sf <- sf::st_as_sf(
  penguin_counts,
  coords = c("longitude", "latitude"),
  crs = 4326
)
penguin_points_sf <- sf::st_transform(penguin_points_sf, crs = 3031)
point_coordinates <- sf::st_coordinates(penguin_points_sf)
penguin_points <- sf::st_drop_geometry(penguin_points_sf)
penguin_points$x <- point_coordinates[, "X"] +
  (match(penguin_points$species, c("Adelie", "Chinstrap", "Gentoo")) - 2) * 20000
penguin_points$y <- point_coordinates[, "Y"]

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = antarctica_sf, fill = "#e6f2f7", color = "#3b6173", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_point(
    data = penguin_points,
    aes(x = x, y = y, color = species, size = count),
    alpha = 0.85
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = penguin_points,
    aes(x = x, y = y, label = count, color = species),
    vjust = -0.8,
    size = 3,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_sf_text(
    data = island_locations,
    aes(label = island),
    nudge_y = 60000,
    size = 3,
    color = "black"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Adelie = "#d72a0b", Chinstrap = "#3f9c09", Gentoo = "#0ca0a0")) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Penguin count", range = c(3, 8)) +
  coord_sf(
    crs = sf::st_crs(3031),
    xlim = c(-3000000, -1800000),
    ylim = c(500000, 1900000),
    expand = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(title = "Penguin species by island",
       subtitle = "Approximate island locations; marker sizes and labels show counts",
       x = "Easting (m)",
       y = "Northing (m)") +
  theme_minimal()
#okay, that is admittedly pretty cool. Let's see what I can learn from it
```

```{r FINALantarctica}
#It seems like the "geom_map" function recomended in the assignment description is an outdated version of the "geom_sf" function? When I hover over a "geom_map" function, the description basically says that one should use the "geom_sf" function instead.

     geom_sf(data = antarctica_sf, fill = "#e6f2f7", color = "#3b6173", linewidth = 0.25)

#This should be a map of Antarctic streams from the ADD. I use the sf::st_read function to read the shapefile?
antarctic_streams <- sf::st_read(shapefile, quiet = TRUE)   
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = antarctic_streams, fill = "#e6f2f7", color = "#3b6173", linewidth = 0.25) 
```
